 Order

The instant criminal miscellaneous petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner for quashing 321/2022 registered at Police Station Kudi Bhagtasni,
Jodhpur City (West) for the offences under Sections 420 and 406 IPC.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned Public Prosecutor and learned counsel for the respondent No.2 complainant.
Perused the material available on record.

As per prosecution, complainant- Deepak Kumar Kakera contacted the petitioner for getting the registration of his car (XUV500 FWD-W6) transferred in Rajasthan, which was earlier registered in Delhi bearing registration No.DL-04-CNB-9381.
The petitioner demanded a sum of Rs.1,13,990/- to meet expenses for [2023:RJ-JD:30348] (2 of 3) [CRLMP-4321/2023] getting the registration transferred.

As per prosecution, a sum of Rs.1,04,990/- was transferred to the bank account of the petitioner through NEFT on 22.02.2022 and a sum of Rs.8,900/- was transferred by the complainant through online at an E-Mitra located in Kudi Bhagtsani, Jodhpur.

The allegation against present petitioner is that from the beginning, he had the intention to cheat the complainant Mahendra Dadhich vs State Of Rajasthan on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/110468738/
1 and therefore, despite receiving the amount, he did not execute the work as promised.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As per prosecution, the petitioner on being repeatedly requested by the complainant to refund the amount paid to him for aforementioned service told the complainant that he is depositing the amount taken by him by way of a cheque No.070420 in the name of his firm i.e. Sumangal Trade Link, however,
the amount was never deposited in the bank account.

From the perusal of the record of the case, this Court finds that learned counsel for the petitioner on 11.08.2023, informed co-ordinate Bench of this Court that the petitioner is ready and willing to return the amount and therefore, he may be granted time upto 01.09.2023.
Having considered aforesaid submission made on behalf of the petitioner, on 11.08.2023,
co-ordinate Bench of this Court ordered that the petitioner shall not be arrested in connection with the FIR No.321/2022 lodged against the petitioner at PS Kudi Bhagtsani.
Learned counsel for the complainant submitted that the petitioner has not returned the amount as promised.

Learned Public Prosecutor also submitted that the petitioner is neither co- operating with the investigation nor has appeared before the [2023:RJ-JD:30348] (3 of 3) [CRLMP-4321/2023]
Investigating Officer, as directed by the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 11.08.2023.

Having gone through the FIR, the factual report of the case submitted by the investigating agency through Public Prosecutor, this Court finds that a cognizable offence has been made out against the petitioner in the investigation carried out by the investigating agency.

Thus, at this stage, in view of law laid down by Hon'ble the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana versus Bhajan Lal reported in 1992 (Supp.) 1 SCC 335, this Court is not expected to examine in detail the truthfulness and genuineness of the allegations levelled against the petitioner.

entities.text: State of Haryana versus Bhajan Lal reported in 1992 (Supp.) 1 SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court also finds that serious accusations have been levelled against the present petitioner.
The petitioner appears to have made a false statement before co-ordinate Bench of this Court on 11.08.2023, only in order to secure indulgence of interim protection.
However, now, he is neither co-operating with the investigating agency nor is returning the amount as promised by him before this Court on 11.08.2023.
This Court is, therefore, not inclined to interfere in the course of investigation or to quash the FIR.
Accordingly, the instant criminal miscellaneous petition is hereby dismissed as being devoid of merit.
(KULDEEP MATHUR),J /tarun goyal/
